symptom: `mxcli check -p` refuses the describe output of Evora's AgentCommons.DS_Agent_GetDeployedModels: "the constraint names GenAICommons.ENUM_ModelSupport._True, which is neither an attribute nor an association of it … CE0161". With --no-check, exec writes `[A = M.E._True]` verbatim and mxbuild 10.24.15 reports CE0161 — the round trip corrupts a Studio Pro-authored retrieve
cause: normalizeXPathEnumRefs' xpathEnumRefRe required every part of `Module.Enum.Value` to start with a letter. Studio Pro names a True/False enumeration's values `_True`/`_False` (the bare words are reserved) and stores `[A = '_True']`; describe prints the qualified name, and the writer then left it unrewritten. xpathQualifiedNameRe (the project-aware path used by access rules) already allowed `_`
insight: A check that looks like a false positive can be the only witness of a writer bug: check validates retrieveXPathConstraint's output, which is exactly what the builder stores, so 'check refuses describe output' meant 'exec would corrupt this'. Before relaxing a reference rule on a describe round trip, exec the same text into a scratch project with --no-check and read back the stored BSON. Two regexes describing one token class (xpathEnumRefRe vs xpathQualifiedNameRe) had drifted on the leading character
